result.summary: This unit is the sentry-native 0.7.8 crash/error reporting SDK: core event, scope and session handling; inproc, breakpad and crashpad backends; curl, winhttp, disk and function transports; module finders, symbolizers and unwinders; plus tests and examples. I reviewed all source files for hidden network destinations, credential access, code loading, TLS weakening, persistence and obfuscation. The code matches upstream behaviour: data goes only to the configured DSN and local database files. The binary jars, keystore and test fixtures are standard upstream tooling and test data, not compiled in.

findings.title: Build-tool wrapper jars present
findings.detail: .mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.jar and ndk/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar are standard Maven and Gradle wrapper jars for the upstream Java/Android tooling. Neither is marked as absent from the source repository. They are not part of the C build that links this library, so they do not affect what is compiled into the binary.

findings.title: Android debug keystore present
findings.detail: ndk/debug.keystore is the upstream Android sample's debug signing keystore. It is not used in the native build.

findings.title: Binary test fixtures read only by unit tests
findings.detail: tests/fixtures/*.so, sentry_example and the fuzzing-failures inputs are read only by the unit tests (test_modulefinder.c, test_fuzzfailures.c) as parse inputs. Nothing loads or executes them, and they are not compiled into the library.

findings.title: Defaults taken from environment variables
findings.detail: sentry_options_new reads the SENTRY_DSN, SENTRY_DEBUG, SENTRY_RELEASE and SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT environment variables as defaults. This is documented upstream behaviour: the DSN only sets the reporting destination, and the embedding application can override all of them.

findings.title: Permissive file modes for database files
findings.detail: Lock files are created with mode 0666 and data files with 0664. Envelopes may contain crash data, so files written to a shared directory could be readable by other local users. This matches upstream and is not deliberate.

data_flows.what: Serialized Sentry envelopes: events, breadcrumbs, user/tags/extra/contexts, OS context, loaded module list, stack traces, sessions, and any configured attachments
data_flows.to: HTTP(S) POST to the envelope endpoint derived from the configured DSN, optionally through the configured proxy

data_flows.what: The same serialized Sentry envelopes as the curl transport
data_flows.to: HTTP(S) POST via WinHTTP to the DSN envelope endpoint (Windows)

data_flows.what: Minidumps plus the serialized scope event, breadcrumb files and configured attachments
data_flows.to: Out-of-process crashpad_handler executable, which uploads to the DSN minidump URL

data_flows.what: Path of crashpad_wer.dll, registered as a WER helper module (Windows crashpad backend only)
Run directories, lock files, session.json, queued envelopes, the last_crash marker and the user-consent file
data_flows.to: Files under the configured database path (default .sentry-native in the working directory)

data_flows.what: Debug log messages, only when debug is enabled
Envelopes written to files for the Java SDK to send
data_flows.to: Outbox directory supplied by the Android Java layer
